newsitem.title: USA: Albright welcomes U.N. reform proposals.
newsitem.headline: Albright welcomes U.N. reform proposals.

text.p: Secretary of State Madeleine Albright welcomed U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan's U.N. reform proposals on Wednesday and said the United States would push the General Assembly to act quickly on them.
"The United States was very pleased to see the reform proposals introduced today," she told reporters.
"We have not had time to review the proposals in detail but heartily endorse their focus on improving management and efficiencies, cutting costs and emphasising the U.N.'s core missions," she said.

Albright, speaking during a photo session with Swedish Foreign Minsiter Lena Hjelm-Wallen, added: "We will be urging the U.N. General Assembly to embrace the movement toward reform that is reflected in the secretary general's proposal and to approve concrete measures at an early date."

Annan proposed the biggest shakeup in the history of the United Nations earlier on Wednesday, promising to overhaul its bureaucracy, shrink budgets, merge programmes and put the savings to work in poor nations.
He became the U.N.'s top diplomat with U.S. backing after Washington forced out Egyptian diplomat Boutros Boutros-Ghali, accusing him of failing to taking sufficient steps to reform the world body.

Key members of Congress have sharply criticised the United Nations for being a bloated, inefficient bureacracy. Over the years, lawmakers have withheld millions of dollars in dues owed by the United States as the U.N.'s biggest contributor.

The U.S. Senate is moving toward appropriating $819 million of the $1.6 billion in arrears owed to the United Nations. Conditions are attached to the U.S. payment -- many of which the United Nations can meet but some of which are opposed by the rest of the world as idiosyncratic.
Among the most controversial demand is reducing the U.S. share of the budget and crediting Washington with money it spent voluntarily to support peacekeeping missions.
Albright said she expects Congress to approve the arrears.
But she also reiterated the U.S. intention to renegotiate with the United Nations, as part of the reform effort, a decrease in the U.S. share of the U.N. budget.
"Other countries need to pick up some more of the costs of the U.N.," she said.
